theme: 3 terms on app colors: the main tint, the color loaded by name, and the catalog entry with light and dark versions

terms.definition: The main color of your app that tints buttons, links and controls.
terms.example: Change the Accent Color to the new brand blue.

terms.definition: A color that you load from the asset catalog by its name.

terms.definition: An asset catalog entry that holds one color with its light and dark versions.

label.textColor = UIColor(named: "Brand")

video.title: Accent Color, Named Color & Color Set | Day 121
video.description:
Learn to explain how iOS apps store and use brand colors: Accent Color, Named Color & Color Set, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Accent Color - The main color of your app that tints buttons, links and controls.
Named Color - A color that you load from the asset catalog by its name.
Color Set - An asset catalog entry that holds one color with its light and dark versions.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

landscape.hook: Can you explain Accent Color, Named Color and Color Set in English?

dialogue.title: Brand blue in dark mode

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, our brand blue looks wrong in dark mode.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: How do you create it now?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: With a fixed hex value in code.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Make a Color Set instead. It holds a light and a dark version.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And how do I use it?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Load it as a Named Color, like in the code.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Does `UIColor(named:)` return `nil` if the name is wrong?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. It returns an optional, so check the Color Set name.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: What about buttons? They are still blue.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Set the Accent Color. It tints buttons and links.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Can I use my Named Color there?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. Use it for the Accent Color, like `tintColor` in the code.
Change the Accent Color to match the brand.
